On Mon, Jun 21, 2027 at 08:44 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding Alex's note and the logs. Initial read: traces look like auth failures at validate stage getting mapped upstream as 502/503/429.

Quick sync from runtime: we've confirmed one path where the gateway returns a generic 502 when the downstream token-validation service fails with a TCP reset during heavy retry bursts. Separately, some logs show JWT "exp" validation failing due to clock skew from a recent VM image with an NTP drift of ~65s on a small subset of hosts — those tokens were rejected, but our rate limiter then surfaced 429s in aggregate.

Immediate mitigations we are executing (in flight):
- Disable aggressive client-side retry guidance via SDK flags for the affected route (rolling out now).
- Add explicit mapping so validation service 401/403 are propagated to the client instead of being masked as 502. Patch rolling to canary now.
- Force NTP resync on the small host pool; revoking and reissuing short-lived API keys for customers that saw rejections (will run a targeted key refresh).

I'll update in 30m with canary results. If this pattern is confirmed, we should treat as a joint postmortem with customer-facing action items.

- Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
